messages.subject: LGCP cluster process
parts:
Hi,

I’m trying to apply a LGCP model to my data using INLA and SPDE approaches, but the results are not what I expected.. The count obtained through sum(cell area x intensity) is very different than what I observed in my data. 
The locations in my data are clustered and I suspect that I need to consider specific hyperparameters for spatial effects and maybe a constructed covariate based on the distance between the points.. However I'm not sure if this is the problem and, if it is, I don’t know how to do this in SPDE approach.. Does anyone have any idea?
My data looks like





and my code is:

library(INLA)
library(sp)
library(maptools)
library(rgeos)

shp<-readRDS("shp.rds")
coords_in<-readRDS("coords_in.rds")

gg<-gSimplify(shp,tol=0.02)

nc.border <- unionSpatialPolygons(gg, rep(1, nrow(shp)))

nc.bdry <- inla.sp2segment(nc.border)


(mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary=nc.bdry, cutoff=0.15,
                         max.edge=c(0.3, 1)))$n


spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh, alpha=2)

n<-length(coords_in[,1])
nv<-mesh$n
w<-diag(inla.mesh.fem(mesh)$c0) 


y.pp<-rep(0:1,c(nv,n))

e.pp<-c(w,rep(0,n))

lmat <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, coords_in)

imat <- Diagonal(nv, rep(1, nv))

A.pp <- rBind(imat, lmat)


stk.pp <- inla.stack(data=list(y=y.pp, e=e.pp), A=list(A.pp,1), tag='pp',
                     effects=c(list(i=1:nv),list(b0=rep(1,nv+n))))


pp.res2 <- inla(y ~ 0+ b0 + f(i, model=spde) ,
                family='poisson', data=inla.stack.data(stk.pp),
                control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.pp)),
                E=inla.stack.data(stk.pp)$e)

pp.rf <- inla.spde2.result(pp.res2, 'i', spde)

summary(shp)
(nxy <- round(c(diff(c(-9.517029, -6.189159)), diff(c(36.961710 ,42.154311)))/.02))

projgrid <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh, xlim=c(-9.517029, -6.189159),
                                ylim=c(36.961710 ,42.154311), dims=nxy)


#random field
xmean_ca <- inla.mesh.project(projgrid, pp.res2$summary.random$i$mean)

#log intensity
xmean_log <- xmean_ca+pp.res2$summary.fixed$mean

#intensity
xmean<-exp(xmean_log)


#maps

library(splancs)
library(ggplot2)
coord_shp<-fortify(gg)
table(xy.in <- inout(projgrid$lattice$loc, coord_shp[,1:2]))

xmean_ca[!xy.in]  <- NA
xmean_log[!xy.in]  <- NA
xmean[!xy.in]  <- NA


library(gridExtra)
library(lattice)
grid.arrange(levelplot(xmean_ca, col.regions=topo.colors(99),
                       xlab='', ylab='', scales=list(draw=FALSE)),
             levelplot(xmean_log, col.regions=topo.colors(99),
                       xlab='', ylab='', scales=list(draw=FALSE)),
             levelplot(xmean, col.regions=topo.colors(99),
                       xlab='', ylab='', scales=list(draw=FALSE)), nrow=1)

#count

cellArea<-diff(projgrid$x)*diff(projgrid$y)

Intensity<-xmean

sum(Intensity*cellArea,na.rm=T)

n



I already tried to consider some covariates, but the results did not improve..

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] LGCP cluster process
parts:
Hi,

This probably means that the range parameter is estimated as "too long". Just so you know, this might be the correct inference based on your model (it depends on the prior parameter for range, and the fact that we use matern field).

You can try to fix the parameter for range to a value that gives you "nice results"
You can try to change the prior for range
You can invesitgate the result$logfile to see if the numerical convergence is bad

I do not think that adding covariates usually helps.

Kind regards,
Haakon

Hi Elias and Haakon,

Thank you very much for your comments. 
Change the prior for range helped a lot. I also tryed to consider an offset term based on the population density and the results obtained are very close than what I would expect, even without to change the priors for range. 

Best regards.
